_doc: verdict of every def by 'path#qual': closed_world mode, and the nodes that differ in library mode. Reviewed by hand against the sources: the items of an inline `mod` are imported with `use` and called by their bare names (utils::{helper, deep::leaf}, `use crate::utils::aliased as renamed`, the glob `use prelude::*`), in the file that declares the module and, through `use crate::shared::common`, in another one; `use crate::top_level` names a def of the crate root that no file module answers: it is matched by its name (weak), never external; `Wrapper::<Vec<u8>>::new()` is a call of Wrapper.new (a nested turbofish). The weak refs of the identifiers inside a `use` declaration are not recorded: they would keep the imported item weakly alive by its name and hide the binding this golden is about.
